title: Maximal edge count characterises the complete graph
statement: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set $V$ with $n = \abs{V}$ vertices. Then $G$ has exactly $\binom{n}{2}$ edges if and only if $G$ is the complete graph on $V$, that is, every pair of distinct vertices is adjacent.
hypotheses_covered: V is a finite vertex set with n vertices
biconditional with G being the complete graph
replaced:
\emph{Let \texttt{G} be simple. Then \texttt{$\varepsilon$ = C($\nu$, 2)} if and only if
\texttt{G} is complete.}
